title: Whitecap Logistics certification briefing
body:
Purpose:
This briefing collects the customer-specific acceptance criteria, pinned prompt ledger, private dataset descriptions, and regression test plan for the Whitecap Logistics model onboarding. Goal is to produce a signed acceptance that permits rolling the model into Dedicated capacity with a canary rollout (10% traffic) and a 4-week quality observation window.

Scope and constraints:
- Model family: transformer-based sequence-to-sequence (customer fine-tune on logistics domain).
- Use cases covered: shipment ETA estimation, exception summarization (email-to-incident), carrier-matching suggestions.
- Data governance: private datasets described below are Whitecap-owned and cannot be persisted in hosted logs. Access is via secured S3/Private VPC.
- Performance target: must meet both latency and quality floors in the acceptance criteria before sign-off.

Private datasets (short descriptions):
1) manifests_2022-2024 (private S3): 120k shipment records with structured manifest fields and free-text notes. Used for ETA/ETA-comment synthesis evaluation.
2) exceptions_email_samples (private S3): 8k multi-paragraph customer emails with ground-truth issue categories and summarization labels.
3) carrier_catalog_snapshot_Q3 (private DB dump): normalized carrier metadata, routing heuristics, and cost bands (for carrier-match ranking).
Notes: data was redacted at ingress; downstream evals use a local evaluation enclave that does not export examples.

Pinned prompt ledger (examples and rationale):
- Prompt A (ETA explicit):
  """Given shipment record: {origin_city}, {dest_city}, {pickup_ts}, {carrier_history}. Predict the expected arrival timestamp (ISO). Provide a single-line confidence score between 0.0-1.0 and list the top 2 risk factors in bullets."""
  Rationale: deterministic structured output simplifies regression checks and enables token-level cost estimation.

- Prompt B (Exception summarization formal):
  """You are an operations assistant. Summarize the issue in 3 sentences, include root cause if available, and add a one-line suggested action for the operations team. Output JSON with keys: summary, root_cause, suggested_action."""
  Rationale: Enforces structured output for downstream routing. Tests include JSON schema validation.

- Prompt C (Carrier-match ranking):
  """Given shipment profile and cost-sensitivity flag, produce a ranked list of 3 carrier IDs with a short justification (1-2 lines each)."""
  Rationale: Evaluates both ranking precision and justification quality.

Evaluation harness and metrics (how we measure):
- Accuracy / EM for ETA bucketing: convert timestamps to day-buckets. Acceptance: >= 72% exact-day accuracy on manifests_2022-2024 test split.
- Mean absolute error (MAE) in hours for ETA: acceptance <= 14 hours.
- Summarization ROUGE-L and human pass rate: automatic ROUGE-L >= 0.38 AND human-rated adequacy >= 88% on a 300-sample holdout.
- Carrier-match NDCG@3: acceptance >= 0.66.
- Structured output schema pass rate: >= 98% for JSON responses across exception samples.
- Safety / hallucination checks: hallucination rate (measured by hallucination_detector_v2) <= 3% across a 500-sample probe.
- Latency SLOs (p95) on Dedicated staging: <= 210ms for prompt A (short), <= 400ms for prompt B (long).
- Cost target (est.): per-request token cost reduction target using quantized variant <= 12% above baseline non-quantized served on same GPU profile.

Regression test plan (execution steps):
1) Run baseline nightly eval (EVAL-319 harness) against the pinned prompts and private holdouts. Collect token-level traces and schema pass/fail.
2) Run human evaluation loop on 300 exception summarization samples (blind) for adequacy, fidelity, and actionability.
3) Spike tests: synthetic longnotes to ensure KV-cache correctness and no OOMs.
4) Adversarial prompts: 200 prompt injections to probe hallucination detector.
5) Automated canary checks integrated into Redwood Console: if any acceptance metric drops >5% relative to baseline, automatic rollback.

Sign-off criteria (who and what):
- Engineering (eng-applied-ml lead): Samir Patel sign-off on test coverage and regression harness.
- Solutions / SE: Diego Martínez sign-off on prompt coverage and integration with customer app flows.
- Customer success / Onboarding PM: Priya Nair sign-off on business acceptance criteria and SLOs.
- Security & Compliance: written confirmation that private dataset handling meets contract requirements (artifact: JIRA-WCL-412).
- Executive product owner: Ava Chen final approval to proceed to Dedicated canary.

Minimal acceptance checklist (each must be a string in this doc for sign-off):
- [ ] All pinned prompts pass schema and token-limits on staging.
- [ ] Private holdout evaluations meet numeric thresholds above.
- [ ] Human evaluation for exception summarization >= 88% adequacy.
- [ ] Latency SLOs verified on Dedicated staging under 60rps baseline.
- [ ] Regression harness integrated with CI and alerting.
- [ ] Data access audits completed and logged (S3 access logs attached to Confluence).

Rollout plan (post-sign-off):
Week 0: Canary at 10% traffic for 48 hours with live-monitoring and rapid rollback hooks.
Week 1-4: Gradual increase to 50% with daily quality checks and weekly human spot-checks.
Week 4: Full rollout if no sustained degradations; otherwise freeze and remediation.

Open questions / risks:
- Do we require an additional privacy-preserving de-identify pass for manifests beyond current redaction? (Action: legal to confirm by 2024-12-01).
- Edge-case: carrier_catalog contains deprecated carrier IDs that the model still ranks; need mapping table refresh cadence.
- Human evaluation cost: need confirmation from CS budget owner.

Appendix: example evaluation snippets
- Example ETA prompt/expected: see EVAL-319 run output (linked).
- JSON schema: exception_summarization_v2 (attached in Confluence page above).

Next steps:
- Finalize human eval pool (Priya) and schedule panelists by 2024-11-29.
- Run initial EVAL-319 baseline on the private holdout and upload artifacts to the Confluence page.
- Meeting: alignment session with Whitecap ops on 2024-11-30 (invite sent).

Notes to reviewers: this is deliberately conservative on thresholds to reflect production risk in logistics (ETA errors compound). If product or customer asks for tighter latency, we should iterate on batcher/quantization profiles and re-run the acceptance suite.
